text: Why should you declare `List<String> x = new ArrayList<>()` rather than `ArrayList<String> x = ...`?
choices: ArrayList is not a valid variable type
Changing the implementation then touches one line
explanation: The declared type is the interface — the abstract data type — so switching to LinkedList, or returning something else from a method, requires no other change. The exception is when you need an operation the interface lacks, such as trimToSize.
